doc.title: Chico Hamilton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Filling in with Basie without music
summary: He played the Basie show from memory, learned from Sweets to follow the lead trumpet part, toured the coast for a couple of months and read Jimmy Mundy's new charts.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Well about 15 minutes before the next show, Basie’s all upset, everybody’s really shook up so they sent for Jesse Price. Remember Jesse? So Freddie Green tells Basie, he says evidentially the kid -- if Jo said the kid can do it, let him do it -- because they knew Jesse. And I went on and did the show. I played the shit out of the show, man, and there was not one stitch of drum music but I knew everything, I knew every chart, I knew every solo everybody played on that band. I could sing all their solos, you know, (musical sounds), and me and Sweets became real tight and as a matter of fact, Sweets really hit me up on how to play to catch the licks, you know, play the first trumpet player’s first trumpet part as opposed to the regular drum part chart, you know. At least you get where the hits are, you know. And man, I stayed on the band maybe a couple of months and man, we went all the way up to Seattle, all up and down the coast right, and Eleanor had just left the band. Paul Gonzalves was playing on the band at that time, and did you know Paul Gonzalves was a hell of a guitar player?
I think his father played bass.

Yeah. Anyway we come back and we have a rehearsal at the Club Alabam and Jimmy Mundy brings in some new charts, right. Man, I read those things like they was going out -- a lot of the cats in the band were scuffling and everything. Man, I just -- things like Queer Street, you know, all those -- I played all those charts, man. But anyway it was cool. I stayed on the band a couple of months and Jo came back and I was cool. In the meantime, I’m working around LA now gigging, you know, just playing -- I become house drummer for Billy Berg, you dig? And I’m playing for everybody, you know, that type of thing.
